blocks.text: Why data science problems leetcode style are difficult

The difficulty lies in the breadth of the role. You are expected to be a software engineer, a statistician, and a product manager all at once. When you face a coding challenge, you are not just being tested on your ability to write a loop. You are being tested on your ability to frame a business problem in code.

Many candidates fail because they treat these problems as pure math. In reality, an interviewer wants to see how you handle ambiguity. They want to see if you ask clarifying questions before you start typing. They want to know why you chose a specific data structure over another.

items: Time loss: Spending dozens of hours on patterns that do not apply to your daily work.
Chronic stress: The pressure to maintain a high level of performance while working a full-time job.
Opportunity cost: Neglecting your current projects to focus on rote memorization.

blocks.text: How to fix your interview preparation routine

Stop jumping between random problems. Create a dedicated space on your Mac for practice. Use VS Code for coding and keep a separate Obsidian vault for your notes on statistical concepts. This helps you maintain context and prevents the mental fatigue caused by switching apps.

Always follow your employer's rules regarding client or patient data. Never use real company data for interview practice. Create synthetic datasets using Python libraries like Faker to simulate your work environment safely.

faq.question: How long should I spend on data science problems leetcode style?
faq.answer: Aim for 60 to 90 minutes per day, focusing on one specific domain like SQL or machine learning theory rather than random problems.

faq.question: Does Lazur help with coding interviews?
faq.answer: Lazur can help you organize your thoughts, explain complex concepts out loud, and keep your documentation accessible while you practice.
